newsitem.title: HONG KONG: China Marine sees container sales up in '97.
newsitem.headline: China Marine sees container sales up in '97.

text.p: China International Marine Containers (Group) Ltd expects to see container unit sales rise 10 percent in 1997 to a total of at least 220,000 TEUs, a company spokesman said on Monday.
China Marine, the country's biggest container maker, sold containers with capacity of 199,091 TEUs (twenty-foot equivalent units) in 1996, according to the firm's 1996 annual report.
Refrigerated container output will reach 6,000 units this year, up from 770 in 1996, the spokesman told the Hong Kong-based newsletter China Securities Bulletin.
The Shenzhen-based company began refrigerated container production in the second half of 1996 at a plant in Shanghai.

China Marine on Saturday posted net profits of 182.31 million yuan for 1996 against 138.90 million in 1995 based on international accounting standards. The company official declined to give a profit forecast for 1997.
Turnover for 1996 surged 48 percent to 3.48 billion yuan from 2.36 billion in 1995 under Chinese standards, the report said. It did not provide turnover figures based on international standards.
Profits rose less sharply than turnover in 1996 because of lower sale prices, the spokesman said.
"Container prices have dropped in the past two years, but now seem to have hit bottom," the official said. He added the container market should be relatively stable in 1997.

China Marine has a 65 percent stake in the US$50-million refrigerated container plant in Shanghai. COSCO Pacific has a 20 percent stake in the plant with the government holding 8 percent, Sumitomo Corp holding 5 percent, and Graaff GmbH 2 percent, he said.
China Marine exported 85 percent of its products in 1996 with the rest sold domestically, the report said.
China Marine has proposed a three-for-10 bonus share issue and a cash dividend of 0.1 yuan per share based on 1996 profits, pending shareholder approval at a meeting on May 17, it said.
